newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-CHELSEA F.A. CUP FINAL PENPIX.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-CHELSEA F.A. CUP FINAL PENPIX.

text.p: Pen pictures of the Chelsea players likely to comprise the squad for the F.A. Cup Final against Middlesbrough at Wembley on Saturday:

Frode Grodas. goalkeeper, 32. Took over as first choice keeper from Dimitri Kharine and is attempting to become the second Norwegian goalkeeper to win the F.A. Cup with a side from the capital -- Erik Thorstvedt of Tottenham was the first to do so in 1991.
Kevin Hitchcock, goalkeeper, 34. Now likely to be on the sidelines, Hitchcock has missed much of the season with a shoulder injury, but is fit again.

Steve Clarke, defender, 33. Chelsea's longest-serving player who moved to Stamford Bridge 10 years ago from St Mirren for 400,000 pounds ($640,000). Solid, dedicated player who has captained the side.

Frank Lebouef, defender, 26. Rated as one of the best overseas players in England, has done superbly well after a shaky start. Kept his cool to score a controversially-awarded penalty against Leicester late in extra time in the fifth round replay. Classy, with excellent covering and distribution skills.

Erland Johnsen, defender, 30. Could be playing his last match for Chelsea as he is planning to return to Norway in the summer and take a job working in a bank. Joined Chelsea for 300,000 pounds ($480,000) from Bayern Munich in 1989. Tall, ginger-haired and another Norwegian international.

Dan Petrescu, defender, 29. A defender who loves to attack - - and also scores some important goals. Romanian international who joined Chelsea for 2.3 million pounds ($3.7 million) from Sheffield Wednesday in November 1995.

Frank Sinclair, defender, 25. A former Chelsea youth player and a member of the side which lost the 1994 F.A. Cup Final to Manchester United, a match he would rather forget as he committed both fouls which led to United's two penalties in that final.
Scott Minto, defender, 25. Has re-established himself in the starting line-up under Ruud Gullit. Joined Chelsea from London neighbours Charlton three seasons ago.
Craig Burley, defender/midfielder, 25. Scottish international midfielder and the nephew of Ipswich Town manager George Burley. A dynamic presence in the Chelsea midfield, can also play at the back.

Roberto di Matteo, midfielder, 29. Italian international who joined Chelsea for a club record fee of 4.9 million pounds ($7.8 million) from Lazio last summer. Powerful midfielder, capable of scoring from distance. His performances have been varied but on his day he is a potential match winner.

Dennis Wise, midfielder, 30. A member of Wimbledon's Cup winning side of 1988, Wise is looking for a second cup winners' medal to add to his 12 England caps. Small and combative, he possesses a sharp footballing mind and creates plenty of chances for the front men. The club captain.
Jody Morris, midfielder, 18. A squad player who has had a number of matches this season, often in a substitute's role. Tipped for a very bright future in the game.

Gianfranco Zola, forward, 30. Just voted England's Footballer of the Year after a series of great performances for Chelsea following his 4.5 million pounds ($7.2 million) move from Parma. Devastating accuracy at freekicks and has dazzling skills in front of goal. Scored a memorable goal against Wimbledon in the semifinal and also scored Italy's winner when they beat England 1-0 at Wembley in February.
Paul Hughes, midfielder/forward, 19. Talented prospect who has played well in the few games he has appeared in this season. No relation to Mark.

Gianluca Vialli, forward, 32. An enigmatic season for the former Juventus skipper who joined Chelsea after leading Juve to success in the European Cup Final a year ago. After a great start found himself out of the team and on the bench which is where he could well start on Saturday afternoon.

Mark Hughes, forward, 33. Welsh international who will become the first man this century to play in four winning F.A. Cup final teams if Chelsea are victorious. Scored for Manchester United against Chelsea in the 1994 Cup Final when he picked up his third winners medal after previous successes in 1985 and 1990. Has had a superb season and was third in the Footballer of the Year poll.

Now 34, Gullit, like Middlesbrough's Bryan Robson, is officially listed as player-manager but has laughed off suggestions he will turn out in the Cup Final. One of the great European players of all time, he played for Feyenoord, Eindhoven, AC Milan and Sampdoria before moving to Chelsea as a player in 1995 and becoming manager a year ago. Won 65 full caps for the Netherlands and when he leads his team out on Saturday will become the first overseas coach to do so in an F.A. Cup Final.
